subject: MAP: Zyphon Health - tokens per $ sensitivity and ops gating
messages:
From: Eli Navarro <eli@zyphonhealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@zyphonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff - cost sensitivity and gating asks

Prioym / team,

Thanks for the intro last week. As we build out the MAP, procurement and our engineering leads need a practical tokens-per-dollar sensitivity and an ops gating checklist we can sign off on before pilot kickoff. Specifically we want: 
- A tokens/$ sensitivity matrix across load scenarios (p50/p90)
- Assumptions for caching hit-rate and how that maps to expected token reductions
- Batching impact on latency (95th pct) and recommended max batch sizes for our 200ms SLO
- A short plan for a canary (traffic %, duration, rollback criteria)

Can you attach a worked example using 10k daily active queries (avg prompt+response 400 tokens) and a simulated 60% KV-hit cache? Procurement will use the numbers for the TCO line item.

Best,
Eli Navarro
VP Product, Zyphon Health
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Eli Navarro <eli@zyphonhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - cost sensitivity and gating asks

Hi Eli —

Thanks, this is a clear set of asks. I attached a draft MAP workbook (ZY-4532_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a short worked example. High-level notes up front:

- Baseline tokens/$: we modeled against our hosted pricing tier and an equivalent dedicated configuration. For the example you requested (10k DAU, 400 tokens/query): baseline token volume = 4M tokens/day.
- Cache assumptions: 60% KV hit reduces generation tokens ~60% for repeat prompts; we also modeled a 20% prefix cache for shared system prompts.
- Batching: using continuous batching with a 25-token median payload reduced cost 6-9% but added 30–40ms median latency. At 95th, larger batches push p95 beyond your 200ms SLO; recommended max batch size: 8 concurrent requests for your target distribution.
- Canary plan: start at 2% traffic for 24h, expand to 10% for 48h if p95 < 180ms and error rate < 0.5%. Rollback on >1% user-visible hallucination/regression.

Action items for our side:
1) Ben to run token-sensitivity sims with alternate cache hit rates (40/60/80%) and attach token-sim-results.csv (in progress).
2) Lauren to map infra footprint & expected GPU-hours vs tokens for dedicated option.
3) I’ll update the MAP milestones and send a one-page “ops gating” checklist for your legal/procurement review.

I’ll follow up later today with the sim CSV. If any of the baseline assumptions above are off, flag them here and we’ll rerun.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Eli Navarro <eli@zyphonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - cost sensitivity and gating asks (sim results)

Team — attaching token-sim-results.csv (summary below).

Summary (10k DAU, 400 tok/q => 4M raw toks/day):
- No cache: 4.0M gen tokens/day -> hosted cost estimate $1,200/day (example tier).
- 40% KV hit: gen toks down to 2.6M -> ~35% cost reduction.
- 60% KV hit: gen toks down to 1.6M -> ~60% cost reduction.
- 80% KV hit: gen toks down to 0.88M -> ~78% cost reduction.

Batching sensitivity (mock latency tradeoffs):
- No batching: p95 = 120ms, cost baseline.
- Batch size 4: p95 = 150ms, cost -4.5%
- Batch size 8: p95 = 210ms, cost -8.7% (exceeds 200ms SLO at p95)

Notes: these sims assume warm KV (steady-state). Cold-starts add an initial penalty for the first 10–20% of traffic; we included a warmup line in the CSV.

Attachments:
- token-sim-results.csv (CSV)
- quick notes in the MAP workbook (ZY-4532_MAP_v2.xlsx)

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Eli Navarro <eli@zyphonhealth.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - drafting ops gating checklist

Folks — I put together an ops gating checklist excerpt below (will add to the MAP workbook):

Ops gating checklist (must be green to promote to pilot):
- Performance: p95 latency <= 200ms under canary load; sustained CPU/GPU utilization < 75%
- Accuracy/regression: no >1% uplift in user-visible hallucinations on eval prompt set (evals run daily)
- Cache health: KV hit-rate >= target (we’ll test 40/60/80% scenarios) and cache eviction TTL observed
- Batching safety: verified max batch size = 8 limits for safe tail latency; implement per-route max-batch guardrail
- Rollback hooks: automated routing switch to fallback model if error rate > 1% or p95 > 250ms for >15m
- Observability: token-level billing, request_id tracing, and per-model p95 dashboard with alerting
- Security/compliance: data retention flags validated, no PSI stored in cache by default (customer opt-in)

Questions for Zyphon product team (Eli/Rachel):
1) Do you have an eval prompt set we can run against the pilot traffic shape, or should we seed one from your support logs?
2) Is the 200ms p95 hard for all flows or only for the core triage path?

I’ll also add a short runbook for cache warmup (staged prefix seeding) and a simple script to simulate warmup during canary.

— Soojin
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - cost sensitivity and ops gating asks (finalized next steps)

Eli / team,

Thanks for the quick turn. Final items and owners below — I attached the updated MAP workbook with the ops checklist and sim CSV.

Map milestones (short):
- 2026-09-07: MAP sign-off (procurement + engineering) — owner: Zyphon procurement (procure@zyphonhealth.com) + lauren_bishop
- 2026-09-09: Canary day 0 (2% traffic, 24h) — owner: ben_carter (execute sims + monitor)
- 2026-09-11: Canary expansion (10% traffic, 48h) if pass criteria — owner: soojin_lee (promote via routing policy)
- 2026-09-20: Pilot ramp to 50% / business review — owner: Eli Navarro + Redwood CS

Key gating thresholds (recap):
- Token econ: show >=35% cost reduction at 40% cache, >=60% at 60% cache for your typical traffic mix (simulation attached).
- Latency: p95 < 200ms during canary; immediate rollback if p95 > 250ms for >15min or error rate >1%
- Observability: token-level billing and per-route traces must be available to Zyphon dashboard before expansion

Next steps for Zyphon: share eval prompt set or permission for Redwood to seed initial prompts (answer to Soojin’s Q1), and procurement to confirm billing cadence so we can attach MAP TCO to SOW.

I’ll push the MAP workbook to the Drive link and update HubSpot HZ-4532 with the milestone dates.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
